newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: M.HILL SEES COST CONTROL BOOST IN 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: M.HILL SEES COST CONTROL BOOST IN 1997/98.

text.p: Jewellery manufacturer and retailer Michael Hill Ltd said on Tuesday the 1997/1998 financial year promised to be a far better one for the group, due to improved marketing and improved cost control.
Earlier, the company reported a net profit for the year to June 30 of NZ$5.15 million, down three percent on the $5.32 million profit the previous year.
It declared a dividend of 3.5 cents per share, taking the total dividend for the year to seven cps.
"A number of one-off costs are behind us. Some new results from our staff training programmes and cost saving initiatives should flow through to the bottom line," the company said.
"The group will continue to pursue its overall strategy of controlled profitable growth," it added.
However, the emphasis will be on improving profitability from existing operations.
"The directors remain confident in the continuing growth and profitability of the group," the company said.

The company said it was satisfied with its result even though it fell short of its own forecast target profit range of $5.3 to $5.5 million. It said the year had been a difficult one for retailing in both New Zealand and Australia.
